summary: This lecture tells what happened after the Prophet ﷺ returned from the Isra' and Mi'raj: he was anxious and sad because he knew people would call him a liar, yet he still conveyed it. Abu Jahl gathered a crowd at the Hijr, the Quraysh mocked, and when asked about Bayt al-Maqdis, Allah showed it to the Prophet so he could describe it accurately. The ustaz separates authentic reports from weak ones, tells of the steadfastness of Abu Bakr, who was called As-Siddiq, and links it all to the courage to state the truth, citing the book Peribadi Hebat by Hamka and The Courage to Be Disliked. The last part explains how Jibril AS taught the Prophet the five prayer times over two days, followed by the story of Mut'im ibn Adi withdrawing his protection, and advice that we focus on what we can control, starting with family.
keyPoints: Courage is not the absence of fear. The Prophet ﷺ was afraid and anxious, but overcame the fear and still conveyed the truth.
An authentic report says the Prophet was in Mecca early the morning after the Isra', unsettled, and Abu Jahl came asking in a mocking tone.
When the Quraysh asked about Bayt al-Maqdis, Allah showed it to the Prophet, who described it accurately.
The stories about the trade caravans, the camel that bolted and the water vessel come from weak reports, so they are not used as evidence.
Abu Bakr replied that he believed the Prophet received revelation from heaven, so last night's journey was no wonder to him, and he was called As-Siddiq.
Jibril AS led the Prophet ﷺ in prayer in Mecca for two days to teach the start and end of the five prayers.
Focus on what is within our sphere of influence, starting with ourselves and our family, and put contribution before recognition.

chapters.title: Opening: courage and contribution
chapters.summary: The ustaz opens with a reflection on courage and putting contribution before recognition.

chapters.title: Courage in stating the truth as a sunnah
chapters.summary: After the Isra' and Mi'raj, the Prophet ﷺ was tested in conveying an event hard for the mind to accept.

chapters.title: The authentic report from Ibn Abbas
chapters.summary: The ustaz explains his approach: the authentic is the core, the weak is mentioned as weak, and what has no source is left out.

chapters.title: Reports with no source about the speed of the journey
chapters.summary: The stories of the bed still being warm and the water not yet spilled have no authentic source, and the event is miraculous enough.

chapters.title: The Prophet sits alone and Abu Jahl comes
chapters.summary: The Prophet was unsettled and alone before the Kaaba; the first to come was Abu Jahl.

chapters.title: The press conference at the Hijr
chapters.summary: Abu Jahl gathered the Quraysh, the Prophet told of the Isra', and they clapped and mocked.

chapters.title: Bayt al-Maqdis shown to the Prophet
chapters.summary: When the Prophet could not describe it fully, Allah showed him Bayt al-Maqdis and he answered every question correctly.

chapters.title: A weak report of Ibn Ishaq: the trade caravans
chapters.summary: A report from Umm Hani mentions three caravan events, but the ustaz stresses it is weak.

chapters.title: The Quraysh's reaction and Abu Bakr As-Siddiq
chapters.summary: The Quraysh sought out Abu Bakr, who replied that if the Prophet said so, he spoke the truth.

chapters.title: Two books on courage
chapters.summary: The ustaz introduces Peribadi Hebat by Hamka and reads a passage on courage.

chapters.title: The Courage to Be Disliked
chapters.summary: The book's view on trauma and contribution versus recognition is linked to the Prophet's ﷺ attitude.

chapters.title: The humility of scholars
chapters.summary: The words of Imam Malik and Imam Shafi'i show that scholars did not chase recognition.

chapters.title: Jibril teaches the prayer times
chapters.summary: The hadith of Jibril leading prayer for two days to explain the start and end of the five prayer times.

chapters.title: Mut'im ibn Adi withdraws protection
chapters.summary: A report that is not authentic says Mut'im, who protected the Prophet, was now shaken and withdrew his support.

chapters.title: Focus on what can be controlled
chapters.summary: The ustaz closes with advice to focus on matters within our sphere of influence, and the Prophet's supplication about truth and falsehood.

chapters.title: Q&A: family and Jibril as imam
chapters.summary: Family as a priority, and the explanation that Jibril led the Prophet in prayer in Mecca, not in the heavens.

books.context: A self-development book written around the 1950s; the ustaz reads the chapter on courage. The ustaz once discussed it every week at a youth rehabilitation centre.
Written as a five-night dialogue; it draws on the philosophy of the psychologist Adler. The ustaz says it is controversial and should be read selectively.
books.note: Two authors from Japan, names not mentioned in the lecture.

books.context: Source of the hadith of Ibn Abbas on Bayt al-Maqdis being shown to the Prophet.
Cited for the authentic hadith of Ibn Abbas and the weak report on the trade caravans.
Ibn Hisham condensed Ibn Ishaq's work; the caravan report is in it and is said to be weak.
Mentions the weak report on the trade caravans.
A biographical dictionary that quotes Abu Bakr's words that he testified the Prophet spoke the truth.
A commentary on Sahih Bukhari discussing the Isra' and Mi'raj hadith and the scholars' differences of opinion.
A sirah summary that mentions events after the Isra' and Mi'raj.

people.role: Companion, cousin of the Prophet ﷺ
people.context: The main narrator of this story; young while in Mecca, the Prophet prayed that he become a jurist and an expert in tafsir, and he later made Ta'if a centre of teaching.
The first to approach the Prophet that morning and gathered the Quraysh; the ustaz stresses he was clever and cunning, not stupid.
Bayt al-Maqdis was shown to the Prophet until it was placed before her house.
Born in 85 AH and the most famous sirah author; his work contains strong and weak reports.
Source of Ibn Ishaq's report on this event; the report is broken and weak.

people.role: Close Companion of the Prophet ﷺ
people.context: Believed the Prophet without doubt when the Quraysh called him a liar, and was called As-Siddiq.
Author of Peribadi Hebat, which combines passages of philosophy with the Prophet's hadith.

people.role: Founder of a school of law
people.context: Said every word can be taken or left except the Prophet's ﷺ, and refused to let the Muwatta' be made a constitution.

people.role: Founder of a school of law
people.context: Advised that his opinion be thrown against the wall if it contradicts the Prophet's hadith.
Delayed the asr prayer, then Urwah reminded him about Jibril leading prayer, and he asked Urwah to verify its chain.
Passed the hadith of Jibril leading prayer to Umar ibn Abdul Aziz through Bashir ibn Abi Mas'ud.
Father of Khalid ibn al-Walid and planner of the campaign against the Prophet that is recorded in the Quran.

people.role: Protector of the Prophet from among the Quraysh
people.context: In a report that is not authentic, he withdrew his protection after the Prophet told of the Isra'.
Mentioned as an example of someone brave enough to be disliked: he accepted Islam though he lost his standing.
Later opened Bayt al-Maqdis and cleaned Al-Masjid al-Aqsa, which had been made a rubbish dump.

lessons.title: Courage is not the absence of fear
lessons.body: Courage is overcoming fear; the Prophet ﷺ himself was unsettled but still conveyed the message.

lessons.title: Put contribution before recognition
lessons.body: The Prophet focused on contribution, not awards or rank; what mattered was conveying the truth.

lessons.title: Convey it even if mocked
lessons.body: The Prophet gathered his strength and still conveyed it though he knew he would be called a liar.

lessons.title: Fear only Allah
lessons.body: When we fear only Allah, people's mockery is ignored, and Allah helps, such as by showing Bayt al-Maqdis to the Prophet.

lessons.title: Don't be a people-pleaser
lessons.body: Excessive politeness can make us stop saying what is true; the Prophet could not call people without being opposed.

lessons.title: Respect without flattery and without arrogance
lessons.body: Respect the high-ranking and the ordinary alike, without flattery and without haughtiness.

lessons.title: See who stays loyal when we are condemned
lessons.body: True loyalty is known not when one is popular but when one is insulted; those closest to a person know him best.

lessons.title: Reject news that tarnishes dignity without proof
lessons.body: When news exposing someone's faults arrives, the default is not to believe it, as Allah teaches in Surah An-Nur and Al-Ahzab and the Prophet exemplified.

lessons.title: The humility of scholars
lessons.body: Imam Malik and Imam Shafi'i showed humility and did not chase recognition, so that Imam Malik refused to have his book made a constitution.

lessons.title: Verify the source of hadith
lessons.body: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz asked Urwah to verify the hadith of Jibril leading prayer, an attitude of the early generations towards hadith.

lessons.title: Connection with nature helps us know prayer times
lessons.body: People once knew prayer times by looking at the sun and sky; today we have lost that connection and rely on apps.

lessons.title: Focus on what can be controlled
lessons.body: Leave aside what is unrelated and focus on your own sphere of influence: yourself, family and dependants.

lessons.title: Family as the first priority
lessons.body: If everyone put family first, change in society would spread widely; a collapsing family is a sign that society will collapse.

lessons.title: Choose who to engage in discussion
lessons.body: There are groups who will not accept whatever is explained; a caller must judge wisely who to involve.

glossary.meaning: A hadith of weak grade, not used as core evidence but mentioned clearly as weak.
The semicircular area beside the Kaaba, where the Prophet stood when questioned by the Quraysh.
A trading party travelling by camel.
The title of Abu Bakr for believing the Prophet without hesitation.
The Prophet's ﷺ night journey from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis, mentioned in the first verse of Surah Al-Isra'.
A hadith of good grade, below sahih.
The start and end of each obligatory prayer taught by Jibril AS through two days of prayer with the Prophet.
Strangers; in the hadith, those who hold to Islam when it feels strange.

dalil.context: The ustaz reads the opening of Surah Al-Isra' to state that the journey took place during part of the night.
dalil.translation: Glory to Him who made His servant travel by night from the sacred place of worship to the furthest place of worship, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him some of Our signs: He alone is the All Hearing, the All Seeing.

dalil.context: The ustaz says the chain of this hadith is sahih. Abu Jahl then gathered the Quraysh, and the Prophet was asked about the features of the mosque.
dalil.translation: Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet ﷺ said that on the morning after the night of the journey, he was in Mecca, feeling heavy and anxious because he knew people would call him a liar. He sat alone in grief, then Abu Jahl came asking mockingly, and the Prophet told him he had been taken to Bayt al-Maqdis.

dalil.context: The ustaz says this hadith is long and he takes only this part.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said that when the Quraysh called him a liar, he stood at the Hijr, then Allah showed him Bayt al-Maqdis and he described its features while looking at it.

dalil.context: The ustaz links this pressure to his fear of conveying the truth.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ related that he was at the Hijr while the Quraysh asked about his night journey, then asked things he did not remember precisely; he suffered a distress he had never experienced, then Allah raised and showed him Bayt al-Maqdis so he could answer every question.

dalil.context: The ustaz stresses this report is weak, so it is mentioned only as an illustration and not used as evidence.
dalil.translation: According to this report, the Prophet ﷺ mentioned three things on the way back: a caravan's camel that bolted at the sound of the Buraq, a caravan that slept with a covered water vessel that was later found reduced, and a caravan that would arrive at a certain time; the caravans later confirmed it.

dalil.context: From this event the Companions said Abu Bakr was called As-Siddiq.
dalil.translation: When asked whether he believed the Prophet's words about last night's journey, Abu Bakr replied that he already believed the Prophet received revelation from heaven by day and night, so this was too easy for him to believe.

dalil.context: Told by the ustaz when mentioning the dispute between Abu Bakr and Umar RA, to show Abu Bakr's special standing.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said to leave his Companion alone for him, and that no one had benefited him more than Abu Bakr, with his wealth and his companionship.

dalil.context: The dialogue of the Prophet and Abu Bakr in the cave recorded in the Quran, 'do not grieve, Allah is with us'. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Even if you do not help the Prophet, God helped him when the disbelievers drove him out: when the two of them were in the cave, he [Muhammad] said to his companion, ‘Do not worry, God is with us,’ and God sent His calm down to him, aided him with forces invisible to you, and brought down the disbelievers’ plan. God’s plan is higher: God is almighty and wise.

dalil.context: The only place where the Prophet complains to Allah that his people have abandoned the Quran. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: The Messenger has said, ‘Lord, my people treat this Quran as something to be shunned,’

dalil.context: The ustaz says this report is sahih, and stresses the early generations' attitude of verifying the source of a hadith.
dalil.translation: Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari reported that the Prophet ﷺ said Jibril AS came down and led the prayer, and he prayed with him five times. Urwah mentioned it to Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, who had delayed the asr prayer.

dalil.context: The ustaz calls this two-day course a very effective way of learning, and does not discuss the fiqh difference over the maghrib and isha times.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ related that Jibril prayed zuhr with him when the sun passed its zenith, asr when a shadow equalled its length, maghrib when people break the fast, and isha when the red glow disappeared. On the second day he prayed at the end of each time, then said, this is the time of the prophets before you, and the prayer time lies between these two times.

dalil.context: The ustaz says this report is not authentic but is important for seeing why the Prophet later sought other places.
dalil.translation: According to this report, after the Prophet told of the Isra', Mut'im ibn Adi, who protected him, said his affairs before could be accepted but not what he said that day, and the Prophet was told he was a liar.

dalil.context: The ustaz uses it to advise us to focus on matters within our sphere of influence.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said that part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving what does not concern him.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions it as a supplication of the Prophet. The chain is not mentioned, so it needs to be checked.
dalil.translation: O Allah, show us the truth as truth and grant us to follow it, and show us falsehood as falsehood and grant us to avoid it.

dalil.context: An early verse of Al-Baqarah about those who will not accept however they are persuaded. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: As for those who disbelieve, it makes no difference whether you warn them or not: they will not believe.

dalil.context: The ustaz links it to the courage to be disliked.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said that Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange, so blessed are the strangers.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions this in the conclusion that family is the first priority.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ said that the best of you is the best to his family, and he was the best to his family.

sirah.era: After the Isra' and Mi'raj in Mecca: the peak of rejection before the Hijra
sirah.summary: Events of the morning after the Isra' and Mi'raj: the Prophet ﷺ anxious, called a liar at the Hijr, vindicated by Allah showing Bayt al-Maqdis, and accompanied by the steadfast Abu Bakr; in the end Jibril taught the prayer times and the support of some Quraysh protectors began to waver.
